Infective Endocarditis Prophylaxis

cardiac eligibility · procedure eligibility · adult dental antibiotic selection

Bottom line
  • Give endocarditis prophylaxis only when both a high-risk cardiac condition and a qualifying procedure are present.
  • For qualifying dental work in an adult without penicillin allergy: amoxicillin 2 g orally one hour before.
  • Mitral valve prolapse, bicuspid aortic valve, rheumatic valve disease and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy alone do not qualify.
High-risk cardiac conditions
ConditionQualifies when
Prosthetic valve or valve repairAn implanted valve, including a transcatheter valve, or prosthetic repair material.
Previous infective endocarditisPrior infection qualifies, even without a prosthetic valve.
Congenital heart diseaseUnrepaired cyanotic disease; a prosthetic repair within 6 months; or a residual defect at or beside prosthetic repair material.
Heart transplantAssociated valvulopathy.
Procedure selection
ProcedureAction
Dental extraction, gingival manipulation or oral mucosal perforationGive prophylaxis when the cardiac condition qualifies.
Respiratory mucosa incision or an intervention on infected skin or musculoskeletal tissueConsider the high-risk cardiac condition and procedure; match antibiotics to the infected site.
Routine gastrointestinal or genitourinary procedure without infectionDo not give antibiotics solely to prevent endocarditis. An established infection is a separate indication for organism-directed treatment.
Dental antibiotic selection
SituationChoose
Able to take oral medication; no penicillin allergyAmoxicillin 2 g orally one hour before.
Penicillin allergyAzithromycin or doxycycline. Cephalexin is an option only without prior penicillin-associated anaphylaxis, angioedema or urticaria.
Unable to take oral medicationAn appropriate parenteral regimen can use cefazolin or ceftriaxone when the allergy history permits. Avoid cephalosporins after penicillin-associated anaphylaxis, angioedema or urticaria.

Pause point. A murmur alone is insufficient. Check the cardiac indication and the planned procedure separately before selecting an antibiotic.

Scenario bank
  1. 45 yo F with mitral valve prolapse and regurgitation, due for a dental cleaning → No prophylaxis
  2. 45 yo M with a prosthetic aortic valve, due for a dental extraction → Amoxicillin 2 g one hour before
  3. 45 yo M with prior infective endocarditis and penicillin allergy, dental cleaning → Azithromycin or doxycycline → Cephalexin is an alternative only when the penicillin reaction did not include anaphylaxis, angioedema or urticaria.
  4. 45 yo M with a prosthetic valve undergoing screening colonoscopy → No prophylaxis → A routine gastrointestinal or genitourinary procedure without infection does not need endocarditis prophylaxis.
  5. 45 yo M with unrepaired cyanotic congenital heart disease, due for dental work → Prophylaxis is indicated
  6. 45 yo M with a bicuspid aortic valve, due for a dental cleaning → No prophylaxis → Bicuspid aortic valve alone does not qualify for dental prophylaxis.
Transferable rule When a case details a patient-specific factor that only matters if the intervention is indicated (an allergy, a dose adjustment), verify the indication. The detail does not confirm the indication.
